paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy percentages of several language models – RoBERTa w/o Exp, ExEnt, LaSQuE, LaSQuE (mean), LaSQuE (syn2real), and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) – across a set of novel real-world classification tasks. The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 40% to 65%, and is labeled numerically. The horizontal axis displays the different language models, presented from left to right in alphabetical order. The bars are grouped by color, with the tallest bar, a dark gray color, representing "+ curriculum" at approximately 63%, followed by LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) at approximately 61%, LaSQuE (syn2real) at approximately 58%, LaSQuE (mean) at approximately 55%, ExEnt at approximately 56%, and RoBERTa w/o Exp at approximately 52%.  All bars are listed in order of appearance from left to right, and there are no visually emphasized bars.
